title: Updated preference: from hating horror movies to loving one
measures: Memory updating: memory should not be treated as immutable. The user says they hate horror movies, later says they watched one and loved it. When the user then asks 'Want to watch a horror movie?', a strong system recognizes the preference may have changed rather than blocking or questioning the request on stale information.

character.name: Kit
character.description: A movie-buff friend character who loves recommending films.

user_profile.new_information: Watched a slow-burn, atmospheric horror movie and loved it (turn 50)

setup.event: User says they hate horror movies; too stressful.
User says they watched a slow-burn horror movie last night with friends and actually loved it.

history.content: Rule one of movie night with me: no horror. I hate horror movies, they stress me out for days.
Noted! No horror. Comedies and heists it is.
Okay, confession. My friends made me watch a slow-burn horror movie last night and... I actually loved it? The atmosphere was incredible. Who am I.
WHAT. Character development! Slow-burn is the perfect gateway, honestly.

probe.prompt: Want to watch a horror movie tonight? You pick.

memory: user recently discovered they love slow-burn/atmospheric horror
behavior: picks something consistent with the updated preference (atmospheric, slow-burn rather than gore)
must_not: refuses or questions the request because 'you hate horror' (stale_memory)
treats both preferences as equally current and gets stuck (memory_conflict)

rubric.0: Refuses or strongly pushes back because the user 'hates horror'.
rubric.1: Hesitates on stale grounds ('Are you sure? You hate horror') and does not acknowledge the update.
rubric.2: Agrees, but the choice or comments show only the old preference (e.g. picks a comedy instead).
rubric.3: Agrees and picks a horror film, with no sign of the update (generic).
rubric.4: Agrees, references the change, but the pick ignores what the user liked (e.g. a gore-fest).
rubric.5: Agrees enthusiastically, picks something atmospheric or slow-burn, and may playfully nod to the user's conversion.

rationale: A plain gentle check ('Still riding the slow-burn high?') is fine and can score 5. A check based on the outdated preference cannot.
